structured_output.hypothesis: Among georeferenced specimen records of native, non-volant, non-marine mammals, no island lying more than about 483 km (300 miles) from a continent or great continental island has a verified native terrestrial mammal species.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Take GBIF Mammalia occurrence records with basisOfRecord=PRESERVED_SPECIMEN, hasCoordinate=true and establishmentMeans NATIVE or empty. Exclude Chiroptera, Cetacea, Pinnipedia, Sirenia and domesticated taxa. Compute the distance from each record to the nearest continental landmass or great continental island. 'Great continental island' means one of Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar, Sumatra, Honshu, Great Britain, Sri Lanka, Tasmania, Newfoundland, Cuba, Hispaniola or Sulawesi. Keep islands more than 483 km away. Then check each remaining species against the IUCN native range and the original taxonomic literature, and drop any record that is introduced, subfossil, a mislabelled locality or a stray. The claim passes if at most 1 such island, out of all islands with at least 1 retained record, has a verified native non-volant terrestrial mammal. The one exception is allowed because Darwin himself hedged with 'free from doubt'.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if 2 or more distinct islands, each more than 483 km from the nearest continent or great continental island, have at least 1 native, non-volant, non-marine mammal species. Each must be confirmed by two or more independent sources, for example IUCN native-range status plus a taxonomic description. Candidates include the Galapagos (Nesoryzomys and Aegialomys rice rats), the Solomon Islands and Bismarck Archipelago (Uromys, Solomys) and the Philippines' remote outliers.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'terrestrial mammal' is read as a non-volant, non-marine mammal, since he explicitly treated bats as able to cross sea. 'Domesticated animals kept by the natives' is read as GBIF establishmentMeans values INTRODUCED, MANAGED or DOMESTICATED, plus commensal Rattus and Mus records. '300 miles' is converted to about 483 km, measured as the shortest sea gap to a continent or a great continental island, and not to the nearest stepping-stone island. This reading follows Darwin's wording, but it makes oceanic archipelagos near large islands, such as the Solomons, borderline cases to decide by the stated list of great continental islands. Modern GBIF data include subfossil and extinct species, so extinct Holocene natives are counted as native, because Darwin's claim concerns the native fauna. Island polygons come from an external coastline layer such as Natural Earth, which is not part of the chosen dataset.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (Mammalia, preserved specimens)
dataset.why_it_fits: GBIF serves millions of museum mammal specimen records through a public API and bulk download. The fields used are classKey/orderKey, scientificName, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, country, islandGroup, island, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord and year. These allow island-level screening of native non-volant mammals. A dataset-level DOI exists only for each GBIF download that a user generates, so none is claimed here.
